notes: WALKED AWAY 2026-08-23, recorded so the time is never spent twice. Cerebras WAS the strongest free-tier candidate left and the UI half of the flow works perfectly: cloud.cerebras.ai -> 'Accept All' -> 'GOOGLE' completed SSO with no chooser and no password (the robot profile was already authenticated), creating org_kwmyd248d63vx6mchd9y239x / prj_8nxpcmhpvpnhkrw2re8jp94d, and the get-started page auto-provisions a key behind a 'COPY API KEY' button -- captured cleanly, csk-...kcv8, 52 chars. THE BLOCKER IS BILLING, not the UI: GET https://api.cerebras.ai/v1/models -> HTTP 200 listing 2 models (gemma-4-31b, gpt-oss-120b), so the key authenticates, but BOTH models return HTTP 402 {"message":"Payment required to access this resource. Visit your billing tab.","type":"payment_required_error"}. The cause is stated by Cerebras' own post-login modal: "Your personal account has been migrated to a PayGo account ... Add a payment method to get a free one-time $5 credit. Free credits expire in 30 days." So the historical Cerebras free tier is gone for this account -- inference now requires a payment method, and the $5 is a card-gated bonus, not a free tier. Per the harvest rule the key is NOT harvested; its entry was removed from state/generated_keys.json so nothing downstream mistakes a 402 key for a working one. Nothing was paid, no card entered, no captcha solved. WORTH KNOWING for the next provider: this page taught two separate wall-detection lessons. (1) The login page carries the boilerplate 'This site is protected by reCAPTCHA and the Privacy Policy and Terms of Use apply.' with the recaptcha AND hcaptcha iframes present but is_visible()==False -- invisible reCAPTCHA v3 scores silently and never presents a challenge, so there is nothing to solve or hammer, yet the bare word 'recaptcha' appears on a large share of provider login pages and firing on it would walk away from most of the remaining catalog. Hence CAPTCHA_HARD_RE + CAPTCHA_BADGE_RE + captcha_widget_visible(). (2) The migration modal says 'Add a payment method', which CARD_SOFT_RE caught inside an open dialog and refused outright -- but there was no card form on the page and the modal offered Close and CONTINUE, i.e. an advert for a bonus, not a barrier. Hence dialog_dismissable(): a soft upsell inside a modal is only a wall when the modal offers no way past it. Both fixes are correct and stay: the UI genuinely was not blocking us. The paywall was found where it should be found -- at the proof gate, by a real 402 from the provider's own endpoint, rather than guessed at from modal copy.
